nodes.label: Evidence-Scoped Read-Only Checkup
nodes.rationale: The app deliberately states only what it can prove from the host wallet surface (connection, NEO/GAS balances, wallet network). Private keys, recovery-phrase storage, connected-app approvals, device security, malware and transaction intent are declared out of evidence scope rather than guessed at, so checklist completion is framed as self-check progress and never as a security score or guarantee.

nodes.label: Host Wallet Surface Connect
nodes.rationale: Connect is single-flight and visibly busy; a stalled prompt returns to a retryable state after 12 seconds so the UI cannot wedge on an unanswered host request.

nodes.label: Independent NEO/GAS Balance Read
nodes.rationale: NEO, GAS and wallet-network reads are issued independently so a partial failure keeps the successful asset visible and marks the failed one 'failed' instead of rendering a fake zero.

nodes.label: Local Checklist Store (miniapp-wallet-health:checklist)
nodes.rationale: The legacy-compatible browser-local key is retained so existing users keep their prior checklist answers across versions; nothing is sent to a backend.

nodes.label: Plain-Text Report Export
nodes.rationale: Copying a report is an explicit user action that writes read-only observations plus self-confirmed answers to the clipboard; it is never automatic because the payload contains the wallet address and balances.

nodes.label: Account Change Evidence Invalidation
nodes.rationale: Account switches and disconnects clear chain evidence and discard late responses so a balance from a previous account can never be attributed to the current one.

nodes.label: Stalled Read Timeout Policy
nodes.rationale: 12s for a stalled wallet prompt and an independent 15s per NEO/GAS/wallet-network read; independence prevents one hung read from stalling the whole evidence panel.

nodes.label: Runtime State Matrix (Disconnected/Connecting/Fresh/Partial/Read error)
nodes.rationale: Every runtime state has a defined user-facing rendering; a first failure stays em-dash rather than zero, and a retained previous value is only allowed behind an explicit stale label.

nodes.label: No-Contract, No-Permission Boundary
nodes.rationale: Wallet Health deploys and requires no miniapp contract: it never invokes a contract or sends a transaction, and requests no payment, randomness, oracle or TEE permission. It also never reads a private key or recovery phrase and never reads or revokes wallet approvals, so the trust surface stays read-only.

nodes.label: Wallet Health Vite HTML Entry (#app / src/main.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Standard per-app Vite shell: a single #app mount, an ES-module entry at ./src/main.tsx, and mobile web-app meta plus logo.webp/banner.webp assets that the platform host and CDN bundle consume.

nodes.label: CheckIn
nodes.rationale: Check-in is creator- or gateway-authorized and marks the ticket used, which is the state a QR scan flips at the door.

nodes.label: Transfer (Event Ticket NEP-11)
nodes.rationale: Transfer is allowed only before check-in; failing once a ticket is used stops a scanned ticket from being resold.

nodes.label: NEP-11 Token Standard
nodes.rationale: Both badge-style miniapp contracts expose the NEP-11 read surface (tokens, tokensOf, properties) so wallets and the platform host can enumerate holdings without contract-specific code.

nodes.label: MiniAppBase Update/Upgrade Pattern
nodes.rationale: Miniapp contracts inherit the shared MiniAppBase update method rather than each defining bespoke upgrade authorization, keeping one audited upgrade path across the contract family.

nodes.label: CancelEscrow
nodes.rationale: Only the creator can cancel, and cancellation refunds the funds not yet released so a stalled engagement does not strand the deposit.

nodes.label: Milestone Amounts Sum Invariant
nodes.rationale: milestoneAmounts must sum exactly to totalAmount, so the escrow can never over- or under-release relative to what was locked.

nodes.label: NEO/GAS Raw Unit Decimals Rule
nodes.rationale: Value-holding miniapp contracts restrict asset to the NEO or GAS native hash and take amounts in raw units — NEO at 0 decimals, GAS at 8 — so callers must scale before submitting.

nodes.label: Contribute
nodes.rationale: Contributions are only accepted inside the active round window and are tracked per donor, because the quadratic matching formula needs per-donor totals rather than a single aggregate.

nodes.label: Off-Chain Quadratic Matching Computation
nodes.rationale: The quadratic funding formula over per-donor contribution totals is computed off-chain and only its allocation result is published on-chain by an operator, avoiding a sum-of-square-roots computation the VM would make prohibitively expensive.

nodes.label: RevokeCertificate
nodes.rationale: Revocation is issuer-only: because the badge cannot be transferred away, the issuer is the only party who can withdraw a credential that was granted in error.

nodes.label: Transfer (Soulbound NEP-11)
nodes.rationale: The NEP-11 Transfer entrypoint is kept for standard compatibility but always fails unless from == to, so wallets can call it uniformly while the badge stays bound to its holder.

nodes.label: Soulbound Non-Transferability
nodes.rationale: Course, event and achievement credentials describe the recipient, so a tradable badge would be meaningless; non-transferability is enforced at the token level rather than by convention.
